outer_3_unbraked_giant_planets_excluding.earth_moon_primordial_vs_present_note: Present-day Earth (23.93 hr, v_obs/v_TEP = 1.063) has transferred ~83% of its primordial spin angular momentum to the lunar orbit via tidal dissipation; its conserved primordial Earth+Moon spin (T_prim = 5.05 hr, J_EM = 3.45e34 kg m^2/s) sits on the small-body soliton capacity ceiling (eta_EM = 0.145 vs eta_0 = 0.129), while lunar braking has relaxed present-day Earth onto the ambient Galactic floor.

mars_unmodeled_transition_body.note: Low-mass Mars (0.11 M_earth) sits in the transition region between the ambient curve (0.099 km/s) and the small-body soliton capacity curve (0.954 km/s) without a Mars-specific rule.

bryan_2020_pmo_breakup_envelope_test.falsifier: Any unbraked planetary-mass companion or brown dwarf with M > M_cap = 0.61 M_Jup exceeding v_cap / v_breakup = (eta_0 / k_MOI) sqrt(min(1, S)) (0.478 at SIMP J0136 S=0.76, and 0.630 at S>=1) falsifies the soliton angular-momentum capacity bound.

terrestrial_moi_pressure_vs_iron_core_sp.mercury_iron_core_note: Mercury (P_c = 24.5 GPa, rho = 5.427 g/cm^3) and Mars (P_c = 24.9 GPa, rho = 3.934 g/cm^3) share similar central pressures; Venus (141 GPa) and Earth (173 GPa) satisfy the strict P_c > K_0 (~100 GPa) silicate self-compression threshold independently (2k_MOI/S = 1.024 +- 0.008, rho_T = 18.6 +- 0.5 g/cm^3), whereas Mercury's low k_MOI = 0.346 reflects its ~70-85% iron core mass fraction (rho > 5.2 g/cm^3).

kic_8006161_hd173701_karoff_2018_solar_t.note: Karoff et al. (2018, ApJ 852, 46) report Kepler sliding-window photometric periods varying between 25 and 35 days ((35-25)/35 = 0.286 vs TEP S_*/sqrt(2) = 0.314), while asteroseismic splitting ratios across broader Kepler Sun-like stars (Benomar et al. 2018, Science 361, 1239) show larger convective shears with wide credible intervals.
